concerns.text: The plan defines the target variable CAPE as a deterministic function of the 3D geometry descriptors (specifically unit cell volume and VdW volume sum) which are also used as predictors. CAPE = PC / (Avg VdW). PC = Unit_Cell_Vol / Sum_VdW. If the model uses Unit_Cell_Vol and Sum_VdW as inputs, it can trivially reconstruct CAPE by definition without learning any topology-packing relationship. This is a circular validation where the predictor contains the exact mathematical components of the target.

The plan includes 'Radius of Gyration' and 'Asphericity' derived from CIF coordinates as predictors. These are geometric properties of the specific crystal conformation. If the target CAPE is also derived from the same crystal's unit cell volume and atomic positions, the model is essentially predicting a geometric property from other geometric properties of the same instance. The 'topology' signal from the SMILES transformer is confounded by the direct geometric leakage from the 3D descriptors, making it impossible to isolate the predictive power of SMILES alone.

The plan proposes a partial correlation analysis controlling for 'atom-type composition'. However, the target CAPE is explicitly defined to normalize for composition (FR-011). Controlling for composition in the analysis of a composition-normalized target is methodologically redundant and may obscure the actual variance explained. The analysis design fails to account for the fact that the target was constructed to remove the very signal the partial correlation intends to control for.

The plan uses 'frozen SMILES Transformer' embeddings combined with '3D geometry descriptors' to predict a 3D-derived metric. In crystallography, packing efficiency is a function of intermolecular forces and conformation, not just intramolecular topology. Using 3D descriptors (which encode the exact conformation) to predict a 3D-derived metric (CAPE) creates a 'cheating' scenario where the model learns the geometric identity rather than the topological prediction. The scientific question (predicting packing from topology) is invalidated by the inclusion of 3D descriptors that already contain the answer.
